title: Geometric cyclotomic action on the completed root sheaf
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $g=\operatorname{Spec}((z\mapsto z^q)^{-1})$ and use the root comparison and restriction/coprojection formula [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport, def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image, def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. On every section $e$ of $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_s=\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^{r+1},s}$ at the final object, their composite is multiplication by $q^{-1}\in\mathbf Z_\ell$, acting through the constant-section map and its recorded map into completed coefficients. No primitivity of $e$ is required. The explicit section formulas are [def-pur-point-cyclotomic-section-data].

source.place: (2.2), pp. 280-281 (root action, tensor powers, duals); geometric convention in Deligne Weil II (1.1.7), pp. 150-151; returned item steps 5-7

proof.text: Let U be the final site object of s=Spec k. For every r, compose the rootLimitAction with the projection to mu_(l^(r+1)). Naturality of this projection moves restriction past it. The equations limit.post_pi and limMap_pi reduce the canonical rootLineMap to its r-th root comparison. Naturality of the inverse-image unit moves the projection through the unit. Thus the r-th coordinate is exactly the finite root action defined by the same restriction/comparison composite.

For that finite root action, the adjunct identity identifies the inverse-image unit followed by the comparison with the direct-image map. Its defining formula pulls units back along the fibre-product first projection. Composing with the specified sectionArrow yields the scheme geometric Frobenius, by the unit projection identity of the map/pullback adjunction. Naturality of GammaSpecIso identifies the resulting section value with inverse arithmetic field Frobenius. Root comparison transition compatibility makes these coordinates compatible.

The Frobenius roots-of-unity power theorem identifies inverse arithmetic Frobenius on compatible root systems with inverse(q) scalar multiplication on the ordinary cyclotomic Tate module. Identify the sheaf-limit section with that compatible system by its root-section equivalences and GammaSpecIso, with the extra order-one coordinate equal to 1. The completed sheaf coefficient action is coordinatewise finite Z/l^(r+1) multiplication, and the constant-to-completed coefficient map is determined by the p-adic residue maps. Consequently every projection of the claimed right-hand side agrees with the coordinate calculated above. Evaluation preserves limits and their projections are jointly injective, proving the identity. No primitive generator is used.

lean.statement:
theorem root_limit_cyclotomic_action (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (e : (purTwistZlOne (point D) l).obj.obj (op (finalObject D))) :
    rootLimitAction D l e =
      @SMul.smul _ _ (purTwistZlAction (point D) l (op (finalObject D))).toSMul
        ((purTwistZlCompletionMap (point D) l).hom.app (op (finalObject D))
          (((toSheafify (ProEt.topology (point D))
            ((Functor.const (point D).ProEtᵒᵖ).obj
              (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} (PadicInt l))))).app (op (finalObject D)))
                (ULift.up (Ring.inverse (D.q : ℤ_[l])))))
        e
